name: Subordinate Clause Density
description: Analyzes the frequency and structural depth of subordinate (dependent) clauses within sentences. Large Language Models frequently rely on complex subordination—using words like 'although', 'because', 'which', or 'that'—to pad sentences, hedge claims, or connect loosely related concepts in a way that sounds sophisticated. This results in an abnormally high, uniform density of dependent clauses. Human writers naturally alternate between deeply subordinated complex sentences and sharp, punchy simple sentences to maintain narrative momentum.
mechanism: The algorithm uses a high-performance NLP dependency parser to dismantle each sentence into its constituent clauses. It calculates the ratio of subordinate clauses to main (independent) clauses, and measures the maximum depth of clause embedding (subclauses within subclauses). If the text exhibits a relentless, unbroken pattern of high clause density—where almost every sentence contains multiple hedged or explanatory subclauses—it is statistically flagged as artificial generation.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing academic essays, research abstracts, and professional reports where AI models instinctively default to overly complex, 'hedged' sentence structures.
strengths:
• Exceptional at catching AI text that attempts to sound 'academic' or 'professional' by artificially inflating sentence complexity.
• Resilient against basic vocabulary swapping, because the fundamental geometric structure of the subclauses remains intact.
limitations:
• May flag highly technical academic writing, legal contracts, or philosophical texts where extreme subordination is a mandatory stylistic convention.
• Requires grammatically correct text to perform accurate dependency parsing; performs poorly on highly informal or fragmented text.
parameters:
Analysis: Syntactic Dependency Parsing
Metric: Subordinate to Independent Clause Ratio & Maximum Embedding Depth
Output: 0-100 Structural Overcomplication (Artificial Density) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 74-82% accuracy. A strong syntactic feature that works best when combined with sentence length and rhythm metrics.

references.title: Manning, C.D. et al. (2014). The Stanford CoreNLP Natural Language Processing Toolkit. ACL.
Gehrmann, S. et al. (2019). GLTR: Statistical Detection and Visualization of Generated Text. ACL.
